reviews.reasoning: The whole-psalm call fits the composition's own shape: the vow-to-petition envelope (opening thanksgiving vow, closing imperative petition) runs continuous through all 8 verses with no internal marker strong enough to license a strophe break. Independently checked against pmarks_Ps.json: Ps 138 carries no selah anywhere in its span, corroborating the row's own disclosure; the psalm's WEB length (8 verses, confirmed against web_mt_offset_map.json) sits exactly at the owner-ruled whole-psalm threshold, and one superscription covers the whole body with no interior genre-label shift. The rejected alternative (a break after the kings'-report shift at 138:4) engages a genuine rival seam, and the rebuttal (no vocative reset at 138:5) holds against the WEB text. citation_sweep, check_marks, check_refs_mirror, and check_web_quotes all clear for this decision.

The opening strophe's inclusio warrant is independently verified: the root-pair quotes given for oshb:Ps.139.1 and, on its answering half, oshb:Ps.139.23 both collate at byte tier against the staged OSHB source (splice-verified, zero divergence), so the claimed recurrence across the psalm's frame is real rather than merely asserted. The span holds one continuous second-person address to Yahweh with no vocative reset before the rhetorical-question pivot opening at 139:7, confirmed against verse_map_web.json and matching the row's own boundary reasoning. boundary_evidence_refs mirrors every verse argued outside the span (139:7 and 139:23 both appear); check_refs_mirror, citation_sweep, check_marks, and check_web_quotes all clear.

The core literary claim is independently strong and verified: MT 139:10 and MT 139:12 both genuinely open (verse-initial, checked against verse_map_oshb.json) on the bare consonant string transliterated 'gam', and none of MT 139:7, 8, 9, or 11 does -- the anaphoric-close argument tying this unit's middle to its own end rather than to the prior movement's close at 139:6 is real. The row's own 'skeleton tier' label for that citation is accurate: collate.py returns skeleton, not byte, for the unpointed form against the pointed source -- correctly disclosed, not overclaimed. One evidence-mirroring gap remains: observed_substrate_signals argues a discourse pivot against 'vv1-6', but boundary_evidence_refs mirrors only 139:6 -- 139:1 through 139:5 are argued outside this row's own span without a matching ref.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative asserts this row's own two halves (vv9-11 and vv12-13) 'share one uninterrupted third-person register with no address shift between them', but the closing verse carries second-person pronominal suffixes addressing Yahweh directly, contradicting the claim at the very seam it is meant to rule out.
challenges.evidence: MT 140:14 (= web:Ps.140.13) reads “אַ֣ךְ צַ֭דִּיקִים יוֹד֣וּ לִשְׁמֶ֑ךָ יֵשְׁב֥וּ יְ֝שָׁרִ֗ים אֶת פָּנֶֽיךָ” -- the words transliterated 'lishmekha' (לִשְׁמֶ֑ךָ) and 'panekha' (פָּנֶֽיךָ) carry 2ms pronominal suffixes ('to your name' / 'your presence'), a direct second-person address to Yahweh absent from MT 140:10-13 (= web:Ps.140.9-12, independently confirmed third-person throughout: the head of those who surround, coals thrown, an evil speaker, Yahweh maintaining the cause). This row's own rationale quotes only the first clause of “Surely the righteous will give thanks” (web:Ps.140.13) and stops short of the clause where the address shift occurs. check_universals.py independently flags the same sentence's 'no address shift between them' as an unquantified universal claim. The rejected_alternative tests a rival split at 140:11|140:12, not the textually-supported one at 140:12|140:13 where the address actually turns.
